# Getting started

In this tutorial you use `@dbp/iso-api-contract` to handle one request of the notes API. By
the end you have validated a request body, built a response that matches the contract,
and generated the OpenAPI document that clients are built from.

You need Node.js 22 or later and a project that uses ES modules.

## Validate a request body

A client creates a note by sending a `CreateNoteRequest`. Parse whatever arrived over
the network with `CreateNoteRequestSchema` before you trust it.

The client left out `body`, so the schema fills in its default, an empty string.

```ts
import { type CreateNoteRequest, CreateNoteRequestSchema } from '@dbp/iso-api-contract';

const received: unknown = { title: 'Groceries' };

const request: CreateNoteRequest = CreateNoteRequestSchema.parse(received);
```

## Reject a field the contract does not define

The schemas are strict. A field the contract does not define is an error, not
something to drop silently, so the client learns about the typo.

`result.success` is `false`, and `result.error` names the unknown key.

```ts
import { CreateNoteRequestSchema } from '@dbp/iso-api-contract';

const result = CreateNoteRequestSchema.safeParse({ title: 'Groceries', colour: 'red' });
```

## Build a response

Every response wraps its resource in a `data` envelope, so the response can grow new
top-level fields later without breaking clients. Validate the response before you send
it, and a drift between your handler and the contract fails in your tests instead of
in a client.

```ts
import { type Note, type NoteResponse, NoteResponseSchema } from '@dbp/iso-api-contract';

const note: Note = {
  note_id: 'note_01J9Z3K8V6',
  title: 'Groceries',
  body: '',
  created_at: '2026-10-18T09:00:00Z',
  updated_at: '2026-10-18T09:00:00Z',
};

const response: NoteResponse = NoteResponseSchema.parse({ data: note });
```

## Generate the OpenAPI document

The same schemas generate the OpenAPI document. Pass the contract's version, and it
becomes `info.version`, so clients and breaking-change checks know which contract they
are reading.

```ts
import { buildOpenApiDocument, type OpenApiDocument } from '@dbp/iso-api-contract';

const document: OpenApiDocument = buildOpenApiDocument('1.0.0');

const operations = Object.keys(document.paths ?? {});
```

Every sample on this page runs as a test in [`01-getting-started.test.ts`](../../tests/docs/tutorials/01-getting-started.test.ts).
